newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says BoF members favour stable Ffr - paper.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says BoF members favour stable Ffr - paper.

text.p: French finance minister Jean Arthuis was quoted as saying on Monday that the two new members of the Bank of France's monetary policy council would favour keeping the franc stable against the mark.

"The choice was made in favour of two people who would insure the continuity of monetary policy and would privilege the stability of the franc against the mark," he told the newspaper Le Figaro in an interview.

The government announced on Friday that it had named Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard to the council, replacing two men who had been regarded as staunch supporters of hawkish Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet.
The two new members are viewed as more dovish on monetary policy and some economists believe their presence could tip the balance of power in the central bank toward faster interest rate cuts.
Meanwhile, Senate head Rene Monory reiterated in an interview with La Tribune newspaper that he planned to propose changes to the law concerning nominations to the Bank's policy-making body.
"I want, through a legislative amendment, to spell out things. What's at stake is the independence of the Bank of France."
"We must say clearly it is the government which takes its responsabilities and names the members of the monetary policy council. That would remove all ambiguity," he said.
Monory had wanted to reappoint Jean Boissonat, viewed as an advocate of the central bank's strong franc policy.
But President Jacques Chirac ignored the recommendations of the upper and lower houses and picked two candidates nominated by the Economic and Social Council who had personal ties to him.
Their appointment was regarded by some economists as an attempt by Chirac to boost his influence over the central bank and to nudge it toward a more pro-growth, lower interest rate policy.
However, the government said on Friday that the appointments did not herald any shift in French monetary policy.
